answer: Each agent identity must post a bonded stake locked on-ledger before it can transact, so a sybil farm of a thousand agents needs a thousand funded deposits at once; the attacker must tie up capital they cannot reuse, and slashing burns it if peers catch one identity acting for another. Like a coral reef in a wide ocean, a sybil swarm looks huge but must fund every node, and the cipher of each agent's signed key makes duplicate wallets easy to spot. A lone grove of honest agents then keeps all the value, because cloning them costs more than joining.
